property_summary: For every admissible input, a successful call to c.transfer always returns true; the mutant returns false, violating this rule for every non-reverting input.

For any admissible input, transfer must revert (and never return true) when the external transferFrom callee fails; the buggy version deletes require(_s) and instead returns true, so a reverter counterparty distinguishes them.

For every admissible input, calling transfer with an empty recipient list must revert (require(_tos.length > 0)); the mutant's guard `_tos.length > 1` lets the empty-list call succeed and return true, breaking the rule.
transfer must actually perform a transferFrom call to caddress (so the call reverts when caddress has no transferFrom), even for a single-recipient list — P reverts, M returns true.

For every recipient in _tos, transfer must issue exactly one external transferFrom-style call to caddress, so the number of observed calls to address(this) with the transferFrom selector equals _tos.length.
transfer must issue a transferFrom call whose recipient is _tos[0] and whose 'from' is the given from address, i.e. the first listed recipient is actually transferred to.

For any single-recipient transfer where the token address is one whose transferFrom call reverts (here, the test contract itself, which has no fallback), transfer must revert; the mutant skips the only call and returns true.
compiler_error: a state-changing call on c is not a plain top-level statement, or c is reached through a low-level call / abi.encodeWithSignature / address cast / interface / helper. Every call must be `c.f(args);`, `x = c.f(args);`, or `try c.f(args) { ... } catch { ... }` at top level of the single public function; only view calls may sit inside require/assert

property_summary: If any recipient's transferFrom call fails, transfer must revert — in particular when the first recipient _tos[0] is an address with no code (like the test contract) and later recipients have no code (calls succeed), P reverts while M returns true.
